items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower and its residue functors
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked cyclotomic PBW/Skryabin and category-O single-block suppliers; the explicit finite spectral and centre computations below introduce no additional choice.

Fix a nonempty set $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ of consecutive integers (possibly all of
$\mathbb Z$ or half-infinite), put $I^+:=I\cup(I+1)$, fix a level $l\ge1$ and an
integral multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ with $m_j\in I^+$, and let
$\Lambda=\sum_{j=1}^{l}\Lambda_{m_j}\in P^+$ be the corresponding dominant
integral weight. Throughout, the ground field is $\mathbb C$ and the degree-$d$
degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra is defined by $H_0(m):=\mathbb C$ and,
for $d\ge1$, by the algebra $H_d(m)$ of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]: the quotient of the degenerate
affine Hecke algebra by the relation $(x_1-m_1)\cdots(x_1-m_l)=0$, with
$\mathbb C$-basis $\{x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w\}$ over $0\le r_i<l$, $w\in S_d$,
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}H_d(m)=l^d d!$ for $d\ge1$. At $d=0$ the basis is the
singleton empty word and the dimension is $1$; there is no $x_1$ and no
cyclotomic relation to impose. The $x_1,\dots,x_d$ commute pairwise in every
positive degree.

**(1) Joint spectral idempotents and content idempotents.** For
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in\mathbb Z^d$ let $e(i)\in H_d(m)$ be the joint polynomial
spectral idempotent of $x_1,\dots,x_d$ that projects onto the generalized joint
eigenspace with generalized eigenvalues $i_1,\dots,i_d$; these idempotents are
those of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
they lie in the commutative subalgebra generated by $x_1,\dots,x_d$, are
mutually orthogonal, sum to the identity of $H_d(m)$, and all but finitely many
are zero. For $\alpha\in Q^+$ with $d=\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$ put

$$I_\alpha:=\{\,i\in I^d\ :\ \textstyle\sum_{r=1}^{d}\alpha_{i_r}=\alpha\,\},\qquad e_\alpha:=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}e(i)\in H_d(m),\qquad H^\Lambda_\alpha:=e_\alpha H_d(m).$$

Because $I_\alpha$ is finite (so only finitely many nonzero $e(i)$ occur in it),
$e_\alpha$ is an idempotent of $H_d(m)$, nonzero or zero, and $H^\Lambda_\alpha$
is a finite-dimensional algebra with identity $e_\alpha$. Its (finite
dimensional, unital) left modules are exactly the $H_d(m)$-modules on which
$e_\alpha$ acts as the identity.

**(2) The supported degree and the tower.** The **degree-$d$ supported tower
algebra** is $f_{I,d}H_d(m)$ with $f_{I,d}:=\sum_{i\in I^d}e(i)$; for
$I\ne\mathbb Z$ this is in general a proper central cut of the whole degree-$d$
algebra $H_d(m)$, and no equality with $H_d(m)$ is asserted. The **tower** is

$$H^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha .$$

It is a unital algebra when $I$ is finite and a locally unital algebra in
general; the ambient tower inclusion is the degree-raising embedding
$\iota\colon H_d(m)\hookrightarrow H_{d+1}(m)$ of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]].
At level $0$ the tower is concentrated in degree $0$: $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$
and $H^\Lambda_d=0$ for $d>0$.

**(3) Grothendieck groups and the Cartan pairing.** For each $\alpha$ let
$D(A)$ range over representatives of the simple finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules and $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ over their
projective covers. The **module Grothendieck group** $G_0(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ is
the Grothendieck group $G_0$ of the category of finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]])
and the **split projective group** $K_0(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ is the split
Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules
([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]]); both are taken block
by block and then summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$. The **Cartan pairing**

$$\langle-,-\rangle\colon K_0(H^\Lambda)\times G_0(H^\Lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad \langle[P],[M]\rangle:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{H^\Lambda}(P,M),$$

is the object-level Hom pairing of
[[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]; its biadditivity
on the two groups is the descent proved in
[[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]], which also shows
that $\{[Y(A)]\}$ and $\{[D(A)]\}$ are dual bases (over $\mathbb C$ every simple
endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$). Different blocks are orthogonal.

**(4) Residue maps and residue functors.** For $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q^+$
the embedding $\iota$ composed with the projection onto the block
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ is the non-unital algebra homomorphism

$$\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad u_{\alpha,i}:=\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}(e_\alpha)=\sum_{\mathbf j\in I_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\ j_{d+1}=i}e(\mathbf j).$$

The **residue restriction functor** $e_i$ sends a finite-dimensional
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$-module $M$ to the vector space
$u_{\alpha,i}M$ viewed as an $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-module through
$\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$, and the **residue induction functor** $f_i$ sends a
finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-module $M$ to
$H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}u_{\alpha,i}\otimes_{H^\Lambda_\alpha}M$. Their
well-definedness, exactness, biadjointness, compatibility with the duality
$\circledast$ of (5), and their effect on Grothendieck groups (adjoint operators
for the Cartan pairing, by
[[thm-adjoint-exact-functors-induce-adjoint-grothendieck-operators]]) are the
content of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]];
summing over $\alpha$ gives endofunctors $e_i,f_i$ of the tower.

**(5) Duality.** The anti-automorphism $\ast$ of $H_d(m)$ with
$s_r^\ast=s_r$ and $x_r^\ast=x_r$ preserves each $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. On
finite-dimensional left $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules put
$M^{\circledast}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(M,\mathbb C)$ with left action
$(hf)(m):=f(h^\ast m)$. This duality commutes with the residue functors by
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]]
and fixes every simple module by the Schur duality comparison proved in step 4.1 below.
It is used throughout this page in the form $M^{\circledast}$.

**(6) Stable and admissible data.** A charge datum as above is used in the
form of its admissible stable realization of
[[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]];
stable range means at least $d$ Jordan strings of maximal length $l$, and
admissibility means $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$ for the origin $c$.
For an integral multicharge the relevant stable realization can be chosen with $q_j=m_j-k+1$ column heights, $n_{\rm row}=q_1$, and $c_j=m_j-q_j+n_{\rm row}$, after choosing $k$ sufficiently low. All $c_j$ are equal, so this is an actually admissible origin, and $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$ gives exactly the asserted roots. The classical tensor natural-module dimension is $\sum_jq_j$, distinguished from the row count $n_{\rm row}$. These hypotheses are only invoked where the corresponding supplier is used;
the definitions (1)-(5) themselves do not assume them.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Per-position polynomial projectors and integer spectra.** The finite-dimensional algebra has a faithful regular representation. For adjacent dots put $\delta=x_r-x_{r+1}$ and $\phi_r=s_r\delta+1$. The native cross relations give $\phi_rx_r=x_{r+1}\phi_r$, $\phi_rx_{r+1}=x_r\phi_r$ and $\phi_r^2=1-\delta^2$. On a generalized joint weight whose adjacent entries differ by neither $1$ nor $-1$, $1-\delta^2$ is invertible by a finite nilpotent geometric series; hence the swapped weight is nonzero. If any entry of a nonzero weight is not integral, move its leftmost nonintegral entry left across all preceding integral entries. The swaps are invertible, but the resulting first entry contradicts $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$. Thus all spectra are integral. For each position separately choose an annihilator $p_r(z)=\prod_{a\in S_r}(z-a)^{N_r}$ from its finite regular spectrum, with $N_r=\dim H_d(m)$ sufficient. Chinese remainder interpolation gives mutually orthogonal polynomial projectors $E_{r,a}(x_r)$ summing to one. Their products $e(i)=\prod_r E_{r,i_r}(x_r)$ give exactly the simultaneous generalized-weight projectors on every finite module; algebra identities follow from regular faithfulness. There is no assertion that the first-position cyclotomic polynomial annihilates other dots. [F5, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 **The content-block centre comparison.** In an admissible stable realization the actual endomorphism theorem identifies $H:=H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(T_\alpha)^{op}$. Choose $Q=T_\alpha\oplus Q_0$, where $Q_0$ is a projective generator of its genuine category-O block, and put $A=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)^{op}$ and $M=\pi Q$. Full faithfulness on projectives identifies $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)$ with $\operatorname{End}_H(M)$, and $M$ contains the regular left module $\pi T_\alpha=H$. No projectivity of all of $M$ over $H$ is assumed. [given, construct, algebra]

1.3 **The exact centre calculation.** A central endomorphism $z$ of $M$ commutes with the projection onto its direct summand $H$, so it restricts on $H$ to right multiplication $R_h$. Commuting with every $R_b$ forces $h\in Z(H)$. For each $m\in M$, extend the map $f_m:H\to M$, $a\mapsto am$, by zero on the chosen complement of $H$ in $M$. Commutation with this endomorphism gives $zf_m=f_mR_h$; evaluation at one gives $z(m)=hm$. Conversely multiplication by central $h$ commutes with every $H$-map. These constructions are inverse, proving $Z(\operatorname{End}_H M)=Z(H)$, and passage to opposite rings preserves centres. The stated Choice assumption is inherited only for the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. [given, construct, algebra]

2.1 **Central content interpolation.** Symmetric polynomials in the dots commute with crossings by the native cross relations, because $s_r$ commutes with $x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $x_rx_{r+1}$ and with all other dots; these generate the elementary symmetric polynomials. Their elementary symmetric values distinguish the finitely many different multisets of generalized joint eigenvalues. Finite Chinese remainder interpolation in these symmetric operators therefore gives a central multiset projector. Its action on every regular generalized weight is one precisely on that multiset, so it equals the orbit sum $e_\alpha$ of the per-position projectors from step 1.1. This argument does not require the annihilating polynomials for different positions to be equal. [F5, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.2 **A single linkage block has no split central idempotent.** $\mathcal O_\alpha$ is a single linkage block by [[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]]: it admits no decomposition into two nonzero orthogonal factors. A central idempotent $f=f^2\ne0$ of $A$ with $f\ne1$ would split the projective generator $Q=Qf\oplus Q(1-f)$ into two nonzero summands whose Hom-spaces in both directions vanish, because every morphism between them is annihilated by composing with $f$ on either side in the two possible orders; this exhibits $\mathcal O_\alpha$ as the product of the two nonzero full subcategories generated by these summands, contradicting single-linkage. Hence $Z(A)$ has no nontrivial idempotent, and by step 1.2 the same holds for $Z(H)=Z(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$: the stable content component is a single block. [step 1.2, step 1.3, given, algebra]

3.1 **Symmetric polynomials in the $x_r$ are central.** It suffices to show that the elementary symmetric functions in the $x_r$ are fixed by conjugation with each basic transposition $s_r$, since these generate the symmetric polynomials and commute with all $x_i$ with $i\notin\{r,r+1\}$. The defining cross relations of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] give $x_{r+1}s_r=s_rx_r+1$ and $s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1$; multiplying the first by $s_r$ on the left yields $s_rx_{r+1}s_r=x_r+s_r$, and the second yields $s_rx_rs_r=x_{r+1}-s_r$. Consequently $s_r(x_r+x_{r+1})s_r=x_r+x_{r+1}$ and $s_r(x_rx_{r+1})s_r=(x_{r+1}-s_r)(x_r+s_r)=x_rx_{r+1}$, so the two elementary generators in the pair $\{x_r,x_{r+1}\}$ are fixed, and $s_r^2=1$ makes the same true for every polynomial in them; together with the commuting generators this fixes every symmetric polynomial. Comparing with step 2.1, $e_\alpha$ commutes with every $x_i$ and every $s_r$, hence is central in $H_d(m)$. [step 2.1, given, algebra]

3.2 **Arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Let $I$ be any nonempty consecutive set and fix a content $\alpha$ and a finite list of residue operations to be performed. Choose a finite lower endpoint $k$ and an upper endpoint $r$ so that every charge $m_j$ lies in the letter alphabet $[k,r+1]$ and every simple-root support occurring in the list lies in $[k,r]$; enlarge an auxiliary stable realization only in the direction of the stable range, so that the added bottom rows of every tableau are forced to keep the ground entry in every column and every added top entry is absent. By the actual double-cut/common-tail compatibility and the contractible-central-corner restriction of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]] and [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], the $I$-supported content component $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the same finite-dimensional algebra as the corresponding content component of the stable realization, with the same intrinsic Specht modules, the same residue projectors and the same residue maps; no whole-degree equality is used. Applying step 2.2 to that common component proves (b) for arbitrary consecutive $I$. For a content supported in the original $I$, every auxiliary letter below $I^+$ has its ground multiplicity $l$, the maximum possible in $l$ strict columns, and every auxiliary letter above $I^+$ has multiplicity zero. Thus all added lower entries are present in every column and all added upper entries are absent. If $I$ is finite, deleting that forced common tail leaves only column-strict tableaux in the finite original letter alphabet $I^+$; there are finitely many such tableaux with the fixed column heights. A nonzero supported component has nonzero $T_\alpha$ by the endomorphism identification and hence at least one such tableau label. Thus only finitely many supported contents occur, and the sum of their identities is an identity of the tower. For an infinite interval each element still has finite support in the direct sum, which gives the asserted local units. [step 2.2, given, algebra]

4.1 **Simple-preserving duality.** In the stable finite realization, the proof paragraph **Simple images and standard heads** of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]] identifies every Hecke simple with $\pi L(A)$ for a standard label. Restricted category-$\mathcal O$ duality fixes $L(A)$, as recorded in [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], and the paragraph **The actual duality comparison** of the Whittaker supplier proves $\pi D\cong(\pi-)^{\circledast}$. Hence $(\pi L(A))^{\circledast}\cong\pi DL(A)\cong\pi L(A)$. The intrinsic block identity of step 3.2 preserves the generator-fixing anti-involution, so the same conclusion holds for arbitrary admitted $I$. Commutation with residue functors alone would not establish this simple-preserving assertion. [step 3.2, given, algebra]

4.2 **Zero components are allowed.** Centrality does not exclude $e_\alpha=0$. Steps 2.2 and 3.2 prove primitivity exactly when the component is nonzero; they do not assert that every positive root content occurs. The stable realization is invoked with precisely the hypotheses declared in the Given. [step 3.1, given]

5.1 **Level zero and the vanishing witness.** At level $0$ the cyclotomic polynomial is the empty product $1$, so $H_d(m)=0$ for $d>0$ and only $H_0(m)=\mathbb C$ remains; this is the convention of (2). For the witness, $I=\{0\}$, level $1$, charge $(0)$, $d=2$: the level-one presentation gives $x_1=0$ and $x_2=s_1$, so $H_2(0)=\mathbb C[S_2]$ with eigenvalues $\pm1$ for $x_2$; hence $E_0(x_2)=0$, $e(0,0)=0$, and the supported component $H^\Lambda_{2\alpha_0}=e_{(0,0)}H_2(0)$ is $0$, while $H_2(0)\ne0$. This completes the proof of the two claims (b) and the level-$0$ convention; the exactness and biadjointness clauses of (4) are the declared supplier statements of [[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]], not reproved here. [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke $G_0$ is the dual highest weight module
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below setting of the tower: $I\subseteq\mathbb Z$ is nonempty,
consecutive and bounded below, $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ is an admitted integral
multicharge, and $H^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the
degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], using its actual admissible integral-origin stable realization with roots $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Let
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ be the column-strict, respectively
standard, tableaux of the Fock data of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]], with monomials $M_A$ and
dual-canonical vectors $L_A$, canonical vectors $T_A$ and quasi-canonical vectors
$P_A$ as in [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and
let $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ be the normalized highest projection, so that
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ and $S_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B$. Work at source
parameter $s=1$.

**(i)** The exact Schur quotient identifies the module Grothendieck group
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ with the FULL integral costandard lattice
$$V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\,D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A\ :\ A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\,\}$$
by $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, and it sends every Specht class to
$[S(B)]\mapsto S_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B$; the vectors
$\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ are another integral basis, the standard
monomial basis.

**(ii)** The endomorphisms of $G_0$ induced by the residue functors $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of the integrable
$\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock action, and both the standard and the costandard
integral forms carry the actual divided-power action.

**(iii)** Over $\mathbb Q$ the ground class generates the dual highest weight
module $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$. Over $\mathbb Z$ the costandard lattice need
NOT be ground cyclic, even under divided powers: the rank-one case
$I=\{0\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$ has a ground-generated integral lattice of
index two that omits $D_{01}$. The STANDARD lattice, by contrast, is integrally
generated by its ground vector under divided powers.

**(iv)** Every standard-tableau simple occurs as a composition factor of a
residue word applied to the ground simple, and the ground crystal component is
exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$.

**(v)** The categorical reachability and rational-cyclicity statements of
(iii)-(iv) do not imply integral costandard cyclicity; the level-$0$ tower has
only the ground weight.

For an arbitrary admitted consecutive $I$, the same statements hold blockwise and sum to the same lattice identifications. Use finite letter cuts containing every charge and finite root cuts containing the selected content and every intermediate content in the chosen residue words. The transition maps append the common ground tail below the lower cut and leave all letters above the upper cut absent. They fix the intrinsic Hecke generators, spectral idempotents and residue bimodules on the selected contents, and identify both integral lattices by their labelled bases. The dual module here is the restricted, weightwise dual, not the unrestricted algebraic dual of an infinite-dimensional module.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The Schur quotient and its simple images.** Assume AC ([F3]) as the imported suppliers do. In the admissible stable realization, the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ of [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] is the Serre quotient killing exactly the simples $L(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; it satisfies $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$ for the intrinsic Specht modules and $\pi(L(A))=D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, these $D(A)$ being pairwise nonisomorphic and exhausting the simples of $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$, while $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. By [F1] the classes $[D(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$. The ingredients are the Schur-functor image theorem, exactness of $\pi$ and the double-centralizer/quotient description of [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]]. [F1, F3, given, construct]

1.2 **The Fock side of the dictionary.** On the Fock side the normalized highest projection $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ is the linear map with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=D_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B=S_B$ with $M_B=\sum_{A}d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ and $S_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A$ at source parameter $1$; the vectors $\{D_A\}$ span the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and the vectors $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ form the standard monomial basis of that lattice, a second integral basis. These are the definitions and the standard-monomial basis theorem of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], together with the O-side dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$, $[T(A)]\mapsto T_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]. [given, construct]

1.3 **The O-side Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module.** At parameter one the parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is identified with the integral Fock module by $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$, with $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, by [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]; here $M(A)$, $L(A)$, $P(A)$ are the generalized standard, simple and projective objects of the genuine block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]. [given, construct]

2.1 **The identification of $G_0$ with the costandard lattice.** Define $\Phi\colon G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\to V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Phi([D(A)])=D_A$. This is a well-defined group isomorphism because both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules with the same basis set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$: on the module side by [F1] and step 1.1, on the Fock side by step 1.2, which exhibits $\{D_A\}$ as a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the FULL integral costandard lattice and makes no integral ground-generation claim. This proves (i) for the simple classes and, together with step 1.2, identifies $\Phi([S(B)])$ with $S_B$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, construct]

2.2 **The Specht classes.** For the intrinsic Specht module $S(B)=\pi(N(B))$ of step 1.1, apply the exact functor $\pi$ to a Jordan–Hölder composition series of $N(B)$; exactness and [F2] give $[S(B)]=\sum_{A}[N(B):L(A)]\,[D(A)]$ in $G_0$, the sum running over the simples, i.e. over $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1. The multiplicity $[N(B):L(A)]$ equals the Fock coefficient $d_{A,B}(1)$ of step 1.2 by the O-side multiplicity dictionary of step 1.3 and the Schur-image theorem of step 1.1. Hence $\Phi([S(B)])=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A=S_B$, and the square submatrix on standard columns is unitriangular, so $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is an integral basis; this completes (i). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, F2, algebra]

2.3 **Divided-power integral forms.** The lower library global vectors $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^\uparrow}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A$ and the form-dual upper vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A$ with $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ span integral forms on which the divided powers of the Chevalley generators act integrally, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; at parameter one the standard lattice is therefore generated over $\mathbb Z$ by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators $f_i^{(n)}$, while the costandard lattice is its full weightwise $C_0$-dual: at $s=1$, $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ identifies it with $\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z,\alpha},\mathbb Z)$. In particular it is stable under divided powers, since the $e_i^{(n)}$ and $f_i^{(n)}$ are adjoint and preserve the lower lattice. Nondegeneracy identifies their rational scalar extensions, but does not identify the two integral lattices. The ground-generation use is the actual definition $V_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)=U^-_{\mathcal A}v_\Lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], specialized at one; it concerns the standard lattice only. This gives the divided-power clause of (ii) and separates the two lattices. [step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 **Residue operators.** The residue functors $e_i^H,f_i^H$ are exact, so they induce endomorphisms of $G_0$ by [F2]. The natural intertwining isomorphisms $f_i^H\pi\cong\pi f_i^O$ and $e_i^H\pi\cong\pi e_i^O$ of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]], together with the category-O Chevalley action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], show that $[\pi]$ is a module map. Steps 1.1–2.2 identify its kernel with the span of the off-standard simple classes, precisely the kernel of the Fock projection. Thus the induced quotient map $\Phi$ intertwines $e_i,f_i$, proving the ordinary Chevalley clause of (ii). No head, socle or indecomposability assertion is inferred merely from exactness of a quotient. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, F2, given, algebra]

3.2 **Level zero.** If the level is $0$, then $\Lambda=0$, the only simple is the ground class in degree $0$, and the tower is $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ by the level-$0$ convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]; then $G_0=\mathbb Z[D(\varnothing)]\cong\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$ is the ground line alone, with both lattices equal to the ground line and every residue operator zero. This is the level-$0$ clause of (v). [step 1.1, step 2.1, given]

4.1 **Crystal reachability and composition factors.** The source upper ground component is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space, so over $\mathbb Q$ it identifies the full costandard lattice's scalar extension with the irreducible highest module. Its highest vector therefore generates that module under lowering divided powers. Consequently every basis vector $D_A$ is a rational linear combination of lowering words applied to the ground vector. By step 3.1 each ordinary lowering word is the class of the corresponding exact residue-word module, with nonnegative simple-class coefficients by [F1]. If $D(A)$ occurred in none of these modules, every such word and every rational linear combination would have zero $D_A$ coefficient, contrary to the coefficient one in $D_A$. Thus some residue word contains $D(A)$ as a composition factor. This proves (iv) without requiring integral costandard generation or transport of head and socle through the quotient. [step 2.1, step 2.3, step 3.1, F1, given, algebra]

4.2 **The maps for arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Fix a finite set of contents and residue words. Choose $J=[k,r]$ so that $[k,r+1]$ contains every charge and $J$ contains every intermediate root support; decrease $k$ further to reach the needed stable range. The Hecke-side map is literally the identity on $H_d(m)e_\alpha$: its spectral idempotent is the same sum over words of content $\alpha$, independently of whether the ambient supported interval is $I$ or $J$. It therefore fixes the intrinsic residue corner $u_{\alpha,i}$ and the bimodules defining $e_i,f_i$. On tableaux the lower transition adjoins the prescribed ground entries to every column, and the upper transition regards the same entries in a larger alphabet with no new top entries. Removing that common tail is the inverse on the selected weight. Column ground differences, hence intrinsic Specht partitions, are unchanged. The actual finite-cut compatibility of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]] gives $D_{\jmath A}=\jmath D_A$, $S_{\jmath B}=\jmath S_B$, $P_{\jmath A}=\jmath P_A$ and commuting normalized highest projections. Thus both upper and lower lattices are identified by their full bases, not just their rational spans. On overlapping cuts these maps compose by adjoining/removing the same ground entries and by the intrinsic Hecke identity; the normalized projections agree by highest-vector uniqueness. Every content, vector and finite residue word fits such a cut. Applying the bounded-below identifications and the rational-cyclicity argument of steps 1.1–4.1 there, and taking the compatible weightwise direct sum, proves all clauses for arbitrary admitted $I$. No full degree algebra is identified with a proper supported cut. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.3, step 3.1, given, construct, algebra]

5.1 **Rational ground cyclicity.** The normalized $E/F$-contravariant highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space. Thus its weightwise duality identifies $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$, interpreted as the direct sum of the costandard weight spaces, with the irreducible rational highest module. The ground vector maps to the normalized highest vector; its orbit under lowering divided powers therefore spans every weight space, as used in step 4.1. This proves the rational clause of (iii). The full unrestricted algebraic dual of an infinite-dimensional module is not used. [step 2.3, step 3.1, step 4.1, given, algebra]

6.1 **The rank-one index-two witness.** Take $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$. The supported degree-one block is $B_0=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ and the supported degree-two block is $M_2(\mathbb C)$, with its simple represented by $x_1=N=E_{12}$, $s_1=-(E_{12}+E_{21})$ and $x_2=-N$. For completeness the whole degree-two presentation gives an isomorphism $H_2(0,0)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus B_+\oplus B_-$ with $B_\pm=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$: send $(x_1,x_2,s_1)$ to $(N,-N,-J)$ in the matrix factor and to $(\epsilon,\pm1+\epsilon,\pm1)$ in the other factors. The eight PBW spanning words are $1,x_1,x_2,x_1x_2,s_1,x_1s_1,x_2s_1,x_1x_2s_1$. The central sum $z=x_1+x_2$ has spectra $0,1,-1$ on the three factors; its Hermite polynomials $(1-z^2)^2$ and $\{1-(1-z^2)^2\pm(3z-z^3)/2\}/2$ project onto the three factors. Each factor is generated by the images, making the map onto an eight-dimensional product surjective and hence an isomorphism by the spanning bound. The all-zero-residue cut is exactly the matrix factor. In degree three an all-zero-residue module would have $x_2=-x_1$, $x_1^2=0$ from the matrix factor; $s_2$ commutes with $x_1$ and therefore with $x_2$, so $x_3=s_2x_2s_2+s_2=x_2+s_2$ has eigenvalues $\pm1$, contradiction. The same argument excludes all higher degrees. The first dot is not zero on the matrix simple. Induction from degree zero gives the regular $B_0$-module, with two simple factors. The matrix algebra is right-free of rank two over $B_0$ under $x\mapsto N$, so induction of its one-dimensional simple has dimension two and is the matrix simple; restricting that matrix simple gives the regular $B_0$-module. Restricting the degree-one simple to degree zero has dimension one. Thus the residue Ind/Res computations give $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$ and $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$, with the end actions zero. Their divided squares give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$. Therefore $\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ is stable under $e,f$ and all their divided powers, contains the ground vector and excludes $D_{01}$. This is a proper integral costandard submodule, whereas over $\mathbb Q$ division by two recovers $D_{01}$. Degree one is not called a corner sitting inside degree two. [step 2.3, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 **Conclusion.** Step 2.1 identifies $G_0$ with the full integral costandard lattice and step 2.2 computes the Specht classes, proving (i); step 2.3 gives the divided-power integral forms and step 3.1 identifies the residue operators with the Chevalley operators, proving (ii); step 5.1 proves rational ground cyclicity, step 2.3 proves integral ground generation of the standard lattice and step 6.1 exhibits the index-two failure of integral costandard cyclicity, proving (iii) and its sharpness; step 4.1 proves the crystal reachability statement (iv); and step 3.2 (level zero) together with steps 6.1 and 4.2 separates the rational-cyclicity and categorical reachability conclusions from integral costandard cyclicity, as asserted in (v); step 4.2 supplies the arbitrary-$I$ maps and full integral extension. No step identifies $\{D_A\}$ with the standard divided-power lattice, and no integral costandard generation is used. [step 2.2, step 2.3, step 4.1, step 6.1, step 4.2, step 3.2, given] ∎

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke projective $K_0$ is the highest weight module
items.statement:
Assume inherited Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) for the category-O, Fock/global and quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below setting, the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its residue functors of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], and the Fock data
with the four bases of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].
For $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ let $D(A)$ be the simple module of the
identification of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
and let $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$ be its projective cover in
$\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$. Work at source parameter $s=1$.

**(i)** The assignment $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ is an isomorphism from the split
Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ of finite-dimensional
projective modules onto the standard highest weight lattice
$V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\{P_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$,
so $\{P_A\}$ is a $\mathbb Z$-basis; at parameter one the source vector $P_A$
coincides with $T_{A^\uparrow}$, and the lattice is integrally generated by its
ground vector under divided powers.

**(ii)** Under the identifications (i) and
[[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]]
the map $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\to G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ induced
by the embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules is the
natural injective inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$
of the standard lattice into the full costandard lattice.

**(iii)** The Cartan Hom pairing becomes the normalized highest pairing: with
the projected simple vectors $D_B=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B$ one has
$C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; these are projected simple vectors, not an
unqualified identification of monomials with simples.

**(iv)** Both residue functors $e_i$ and $f_i$ on projective modules induce
operators on $K_0$ that are the Chevalley operators adjoint to their $G_0$
operators of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]].

**(v)** The left adjoint $\pi^*$ of the Schur quotient is right exact on all
modules, sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives and recovers the
standard-labelled prinjectives; exactness of $\pi^*$ on arbitrary modules is
neither asserted nor needed.

For an arbitrary admitted consecutive $I$, use the compatible finite cuts and the intrinsic Hecke identity of the $G_0$ theorem. They identify the projective covers and the lower integral basis $P_A$ on every selected content. Consequently (i)–(iv) hold for the full supported tower, including unbounded intervals; clause (v) concerns the Schur functor in each actual stable realization.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The split $K_0$ basis of covers.** Every simple finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-module has a projective cover, unique up to isomorphism, and the classes $[Y(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, of the covers of the simples $D(A)$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the split Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules; this is [F1] applied block by block and summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$. [F1, given, construct]

1.2 **The left adjoint on projectives.** The Schur quotient $\pi$ has a left adjoint $\pi^*$ which is right exact on all modules and sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $\pi^*(Y(A))=P(A)$ and $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so $\pi^*$ recovers the standard-labelled prinjectives, and its exactness on arbitrary modules is not needed. These are the statements of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]]. [given, construct]

1.3 **The standard lattice and its ground generation.** The standard lattice $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ has $\mathbb Z$-basis $\{P_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$, the source vector $P_A$ lies in the highest constituent with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}P_A=P_A$, and at parameter one $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}=G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)$, so $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ is integrally generated by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators: the actual lower lattice is $V_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)=U^-_{\mathcal A}v_\Lambda$ by [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. This is the parameter-one specialization of [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], together with the basis statements of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]. [given, algebra]

2.1 **The identification $K_0\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$.** Define $\Psi$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Psi([Y(A)])=P_A$; by step 1.3 both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules on the same index set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, so $\Psi$ is a group isomorphism onto $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, giving (i). The identification is realized functorially by $\pi^*$: step 1.2 shows that on projective classes the composite of $\pi^*$ with the category-O identification $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$ at parameter one (the projective half of the tableau $K_0$/Fock identification of [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]], proved in [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]) is $\Psi$, so no exactness of $\pi^*$ on non-projectives is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, given, construct]

3.1 **The inclusion is the lattice inclusion.** The embedding of projectives into all finite-dimensional modules induces a map on Grothendieck groups; in the category of finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-modules a projective class $[Y(A)]$ maps to the class of the same module, which under the identification $\Phi$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] is the costandard coordinate vector of the module $Y(A)$. By step 1.2, $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so this vector equals the image of $[P(A)]$ under the exact quotient, namely $P_A$ by step 1.3. Hence the composite $\Phi\circ(\text{inclusion})\circ\Psi^{-1}$ is the identity on the basis $\{P_A\}$, i.e. the natural inclusion $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}\hookrightarrow V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$. It is injective because the vectors $P_A$ are linearly independent in the rational highest module, and hence also as elements of its full costandard lattice. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space; no claim that the embedded standard and costandard lattices coincide is used. This proves (ii). [step 1.3, step 2.1, given, algebra]

3.2 **The Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing.** By [F2] the Cartan pairing descends to $K_0\times G_0$ and pairs the two bases dually; under the identifications of step 2.1 and of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the value on basis vectors is computed on the Fock side, where the pairing between the standard and costandard families at parameter one is the normalized highest pairing $C_0$ with $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ by [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. This proves (iii); in particular the costandard vectors entering the pairing are the projected simples $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B=D_B$, not unprojected monomials. [step 2.1, F2, given, algebra]

4.1 **Chevalley operators on $K_0$.** Use the actual exact residue biadjunction from the tower supplier. For projective $P$ over the source, $\operatorname{Hom}(f_iP,-)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,e_i-)$ is exact, so $f_iP$ is projective; for projective $Q$ over the target, $\operatorname{Hom}(e_iQ,-)=\operatorname{Hom}(Q,f_i-)$ is exact, so $e_iQ$ is projective. Applying an idempotent by itself would not prove projectivity over a different algebra. These functors induce the adjoint operators of [F3] under the Hom pairing. Their $G_0$ counterparts are the already identified Chevalley operators, and the normalized highest pairing makes $e_i,f_i$ adjoint, so the same identification holds on $K_0$. [step 1.2, step 3.2, F3, given, algebra]

5.1 **The full integral extension.** The arbitrary-$I$ construction of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] fixes each selected finite-dimensional algebra $H_\alpha^\Lambda$, its simple labels and residue bimodules. An algebra identity fixes projective covers of the identified simples, uniquely up to isomorphism, so it fixes their split-$K_0$ basis. The lower lattice map is $P_A\mapsto P_{\jmath A}$ under the same common-ground-tail label map; the actual lower/global cut compatibility makes this an integral basis identification commuting with divided powers and with the pairing against the full upper basis. It therefore transports $\Psi$, the Cartan map and its pairing on each content; overlaps agree by the intrinsic algebra identity and the composable tail maps. Their weightwise direct sum proves (i)–(iv) for every admitted consecutive $I$, without claiming integral ground cyclicity for the costandard lattice. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, given, construct, algebra]

6.1 **Conclusion.** Step 2.1 proves (i), step 3.1 proves the lattice-inclusion statement (ii), step 3.2 proves the pairing statement (iii) with its projected-simple qualification, step 4.1 proves (iv), step 5.1 gives their full integral arbitrary-$I$ extension, and the properties of the right-exact left adjoint stated in step 1.2 are exactly the assertion (v); at no point is exactness of $\pi^*$ on arbitrary modules, or a recovery of all category-O projectives, assumed. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, given] ∎

items.title: The degenerate Ariki categorification theorem
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a nonempty set of consecutive
integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and integral
multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ in the letter alphabet $I^+$. Use the actual admissible integral-origin stable realization of the tower definition, with roots $c_j+q_j-n_{\rm row}=m_j$. Then the two identifications of the preceding
theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower
$H^\Lambda$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]:
$K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and
$G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with
$[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the
Cartan and Shapovalov pairings. Moreover:

**(i)** for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has
$[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$, where
$d_{A,B}(s)\in\mathbb Z[s]$ is defined by $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$
(equivalently $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$);

**(ii)** the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$
$(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of
$\dot U_{\mathbb Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+})$;

**(iii)** for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $i\in I$ the module $e_iD(A)$
(resp. $f_iD(A)$) is nonzero if and only if $\tilde e_i(A)\ne\varnothing$
(resp. $\tilde f_i(A)\ne\varnothing$), in which case it is a self-dual
indecomposable module with irreducible socle and head isomorphic to
$D(\tilde e_i(A))$ (resp. $D(\tilde f_i(A))$);

**(iv)** in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the
quasi-canonical family $P_A$, which at parameter one equals the canonical
family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the
simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family
$D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$, the label bijections being $\uparrow:\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and its inverse rectification $\downarrow:\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For any admitted consecutive $I$, including $\mathbb Z$ and half-infinite sets,
the same blockwise statements hold: for a fixed $\alpha$ and finite list of
residue operations choose lower and upper cuts whose LETTER alphabet contains
every charge and whose ROOT interval contains the support of $\alpha$ and the
required shifted supports; added bottom tails are common ground and added top
entries are absent, and the double-cut compatibility and the
contractible-central-corner restriction identify these SAME Hecke blocks,
intrinsic Spechts, projective/simple labels and residue maps. These compatible
finite pieces give the original arbitrary-$I$ statement. At level $0$ only
$\alpha=0$ and the ground survive.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Both identifications and their duality.** By [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] the map $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$ identifies $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$ with the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and is compatible with the standard classes $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$; by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]] the map $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ identifies $K_0(\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda))$ with the standard lattice $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, the embedding of projectives induces the lattice inclusion, and the Cartan pairing is the normalized highest pairing $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ of [[lem-the-fock-pairing-matches-projective-simple-and-standard-costandard-pairings]]. Since the two lattice identifications are the actual source dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]] at parameter one, the identifications hold simultaneously and are mutually dual. [F2, given, algebra]

1.2 **The actual surviving-head calculation.** Fix $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and let $M=f_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$, or $M=e_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$. The local residue theorem [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] says $M=0$ exactly when the corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise its head is the simple $L(C)$ at that edge, and it is self-dual. The ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ is closed under the two crystal operators by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], so $C$ is standard. The actual detector/corner Hom comparison of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]] applies to maps from a Std-head object to a Std-socle object. Applying it to $M$ and $L(B)$ for each standard $B$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_H(\pi M,D(B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,L(B))$, of dimension $\delta_{CB}$. Since the $D(B)$ are the complete distinct Hecke simples, this computes the head of $\pi M$ as the single simple $D(C)$ and proves $\pi M\ne0$. The natural intertwining of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]] identifies $\pi M$ with the appropriate Hecke translate of $D(A)$, and its natural duality comparison makes that translate self-dual. Its socle is therefore also $D(C)$. A direct sum of two nonzero finite-length modules has at least two nonzero simple head summands, so a module with simple head is indecomposable. If the edge is absent the translate is zero by the same natural isomorphism. This proves (iii) in both directions by a Hom calculation; no arbitrary head or socle preservation by an exact quotient is assumed. [F2, given, construct, algebra]

1.3 **The parameter-one normalization and label bijections.** At parameter one the quasi-canonical family satisfies $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ and the costandard family is $D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ with $A\mapsto A^\uparrow$ the inverse rectification from standard to reverse-standard tableaux and $\downarrow$ the rectification in the opposite direction, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]] and [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]; this gives (iv). [F2, given, algebra]

1.4 **Level zero.** For level $0$ the tower has $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ and $H^\Lambda_d=0$ for $d>0$ by the level-zero convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], so only $\alpha=0$ and the ground class remain, consistently with the two identifications being the rank-one lattices $\mathbb ZP_\varnothing=\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$. [given]

2.1 **The decomposition formula (i).** The formula $[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$ for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is the standard-class half of the identification of step 1.1; the coefficient dictionary $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$, $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$ is that of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and the full polynomial transition matrix, its unitriangularity and the restriction to standard simple labels are those of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]. This proves (i); no off-standard label is made a simple class. [step 1.1, F1, given, algebra]

2.2 **The Chevalley operators (ii).** The residue operators on $G_0$ are the Chevalley operators by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]], and the corresponding statement on $K_0$ for projective classes is [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]]; on the category-O side both statements are the integrable Fock action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] transferred by the actual natural residue comparisons. This proves (ii). [step 1.1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

2.3 **Arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Let $I$ be any nonempty consecutive set (possibly unbounded above or below), fix a content $\alpha$ and a finite list of residue operations, and choose a finite lower endpoint $k$ and upper endpoint $r$ so that the LETTER alphabet $[k,r+1]$ contains every charge and the ROOT interval $[k,r]$ contains the support of $\alpha$ and every shifted support occurring in the operations. The common-tail and double-cut compatibility of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], together with the contractible-central-corner restriction of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], shows that added bottom occupancy is maximal in every column (so every new entry is forced ground) and added top occupancy is zero, and that the monomial, bar, global and projected basis equations are unchanged on the selected finite weight set. Hence the Hecke block is the same content component of the same $H_d(m)$, with the same intrinsic Specht modules, projective and simple labels, residue projectors and residue maps, and the blockwise statements of (i)-(iv) glue along these compatible finite pieces to give the arbitrary-$I$ statement. At the level of the block decomposition of the tower, the excluded blocks for $I\ne\mathbb Z$ are real (the supported cut is proper by [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]), and no equality of $H^\Lambda$ with $\bigoplus_dH_d(m)$ is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, given, algebra]

3.1 **Conclusion.** Step 1.1 assembles the simultaneous full upper/lower integral lattice identifications and their perfect mutual pairing; step 1.2 proves the residue head/socle/indecomposability rule; step 1.3 proves the parameter-one normalization with its correctly directed label bijections; steps 2.1–2.2 prove the decomposition formula and Chevalley action; step 2.3 glues the actual same-block and full-basis maps for arbitrary consecutive $I$; and step 1.4 gives the level-zero ground line. These are all clauses of the statement. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, given] ∎

items.title: The degenerate and nondegenerate Ariki theorems have distinct parameter ranges
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Schur and
highest-weight/global-basis suppliers. The explicit finite spectral and
algebra-transport constructions introduce no additional choice.

The degenerate theorem [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]] concerns the
tower over $\mathbb C$ with integral multicharge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$,
additive cyclotomic roots $m_j$ and the $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$
Fock/highest-weight data. Its integral Grothendieck-group, projective/simple,
standard-class and decomposition-number identifications are ungraded at the
basis parameter one. This parameter is independent of the numerical
nondegenerate Hecke parameter $\xi$.

In the **generic branch**, let $\xi\in\mathbb C^\times$ have infinite
multiplicative order and let $\mathbf m=(m_1,\ldots,m_l)$ be any finite ordered
integral multicharge, including repeated charges. Put $Q_j=\xi^{m_j}$.
Residues are integers and the datum is the directed line $i\to i+1$, of type
$A_\infty$ and quantum characteristic $e=0$. The actual word-preserving
tower isomorphism constructed through the common integer-line KLR algebra
identifies the degenerate and generic nondegenerate categorifications,
including their full integral based families and their standard classes.
At a primitive $e$-th root of unity $\xi\ne1$, the residue datum is instead
cyclic affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, with a double edge at $e=2$; that theorem
requires its own comparison and categorification. It does not follow by
specializing the generic tower isomorphism.

Their inverse composites fix words, dots and crossings, with the prescribed right-side order of their series. This gives the actual maps $\phi_d^{\deg},\phi_d^\xi$ and hence $\Theta_d$; no arbitrary rankwise isomorphism is selected. Their local series are independent of rank, charge order and window. The prefix projector is the sum over its appended colors, so the tower maps agree; the common last-color idempotent identifies the two induction bimodules by $a\epsilon_i\otimes v\mapsto\Theta_{d+1}(a)\epsilon_i\otimes v$, and identifies the restrictions. Applying the exact primary word projector to this flag counts each matching factor once and every nonmatching factor zero, even when distinct tableaux give the same word. Star fixes every $X_r$, so right-to-left conversion preserves these dimensions. Hence $\operatorname{ch}_\xi S_\xi( oldsymbol\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}( oldsymbol\mu)}[\operatorname{res}_{\mathbf m}(T)]$. [F1, F2, algebra]

The affine PBW basis of [F3], read also in reverse order through its generator-fixing anti-involution, makes the affine algebra free as a right affine Young-subalgebra module on the distinguished finite shuffles $w\in S_d/W_P$. Thus the actual induced standard has basis $w\otimes v$, where $v$ is a tensor of ordinary Specht eigenvectors. The mixed relation moves a polynomial generator through the shuffle as $x_rw=wx_{w^{-1}(r)}+\sum_{\ell(u)<\ell(w)}c_uu$: each scalar correction deletes a crossing. Reducing $u$ to its minimal Young-coset representative cannot increase length. Therefore the shuffle-length filtration is stable under all commuting $x_r$, and its factors have the permuted component eigenwords $m_j+c-r$ of [F3]. Each component standard-tableau tuple and order-preserving shuffle specifies one standard multitableau, and conversely a multitableau recovers that tuple and shuffle by local renumbering. Under the projective highest-weight theorem [F4], the classes of these words span each rationalized $K_0$ weight: the lower lattice is ground-generated under divided powers, and over $\mathbb Q$ each divided power is an ordinary power divided by a factorial. Therefore an integral $G_0$ class of zero character pairs to zero with every projective cover. The integral dual bases in [F5] make every simple coefficient zero, proving word-character injectivity on $G_0$, not just on its rationalization. Only the lower projective lattice is used for this spanning argument; integral ground cyclicity of the full upper lattice is not assumed. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **Exact standard classes and charge order.** Step 1.1 makes pullback preserve every word coefficient. Steps 1.2–2.1 give equal characters for $\mathcal E_dS_\xi( oldsymbol\mu)$ and $S_{\deg}( oldsymbol\mu)$, and step 2.2 gives their equality in integral $G_0$. A simultaneous permutation of charges and partitions bijects their standard tableaux without changing a residue word, so it preserves both character sums and, by step 2.2, the degenerate standard class. Sort these pairs into the source charge order. The entries $m_j+1-r+\mu_r^{(j)}$ are strictly decreasing down the column and have the ground tail; their ground differences are exactly the component partitions. The source Schur/Fock dictionary [F3, F4] therefore sends the sorted standard class to $S_{B_{ oldsymbol\mu}}$. This proves the stated generic standard-class dictionary for every finite integral charge order. The calculation uses the same-shape Murphy cell and its star conversion. A convention using a contragredient dual has the same primary dimensions because star fixes the polynomial generators; a signed-conjugate convention must also carry its sign and charge/reflected-residue change. No untwisted conjugate module or unchanged signed residue word is inferred. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 **Transfer the full based and pairing data.** An algebra isomorphism gives an exact equivalence and a Hom bijection on every pair. Thus it takes simples to simples, indecomposable projectives to indecomposable projectives and projective covers to the corresponding covers, defining precisely $D_\xi(A)$ and $Y_\xi(A)$. It preserves the Cartan pairing and the inclusion of projective classes into module classes. Composing with [F4] therefore transfers the full lower and restricted upper integral lattices, their normalized canonical/dual-canonical families at $s=1$, and the Cartan map as their lattice inclusion. The bimodule maps in step 1.1 transfer the Chevalley actions, and the integral divided-power actions transfer under these integral group isomorphisms. Combining step 3.1 with the degenerate standard multiplicities of [F4] gives $[S_\xi( oldsymbol\mu):D_\xi(A)]=d_{A,B_{ oldsymbol\mu}}(1)$. This coefficient comparison is in the transported simple basis and implies neither a Specht-module isomorphism nor a same-shape cellular-head identification. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 **All compatible cuts and all ranks.** On a content $\alpha$, the sum of word projectors with that content is preserved by $\Theta_d$, as is the central sum over words in any supported interval $I$. Hence the same comparison restricts to the same supported finite content algebras and to their residue corners. For any selected finite list of contents and operations, choose lower/upper letter and root cuts containing all charges, content supports and intermediate supports; [F1] permits a common finite generic window, and [F4] identifies the actual degenerate finite-cut based lattices and standards by their common-ground-tail labels. The inverse dictionaries use fixed pair series, so the tower isomorphisms agree on overlaps. The unchanged intrinsic affine standards and their corner projections have the same characters and classes there. Thus their standard, simple and projective classes, pairings and integral lower/upper bases glue under the same composable tail maps, proving the full arbitrary-consecutive-$I$ assertion weight by weight. No proper supported cut becomes the whole rank algebra. At rank zero both maps are the identity on $\mathbb C$, with the empty word, tableau and standard. At level zero the first cyclotomic polynomial is $1$, so both positive-rank algebras and all residue operations are zero, and only the ground line remains. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **The root-of-unity obstruction and characteristic boundary.** For level one with charge zero and $d=2$, the degenerate presentation gives $x_1=0$, $x_2=s_1$ and $s_1^2=1$, hence $H_2^{\deg}\cong\mathbb C[S_2]\cong\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$. At $\xi=-1$ the nondegenerate level-one presentation gives $X_1=1$, $X_2=-T_1^2$ and $(T_1+1)^2=0$, hence $H_2^{-1}\cong\mathbb C[T_1]/((T_1+1)^2)$. Its class $T_1+1$ is nonzero and nilpotent, whereas the product of two fields has no nonzero nilpotent. These algebras are therefore not isomorphic. Moreover, the generic local inverse series rely on $\xi^a-\xi^b
e0$ for distinct integers; these constants can vanish at a root of unity, so the proved generic inverse maps cannot simply be specialized there. The cyclic characteristic-zero and positive-characteristic assertions retain their own parameters and suppliers, and the grading/basis variable is never identified with the numerical $\xi$. This proves the stated obstruction and all comparison claims without claiming a general positive-characteristic decomposition formula. The only choice is the inherited AC in [F4]; the remaining constructions use finite data. [F1, F4, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: Degenerate Specht decomposition numbers are canonical basis coefficients at one
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the category-O, Fock/global and Schur quotient suppliers invoked below.

Use the actual source chart at parameter $s$: with the monomials $M_A$ and the
dual-canonical vectors $L_A$ of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], put

$$R_{A,B}(s)=p_{A,B}(-s),\qquad L_B=\sum_AR_{A,B}(s)M_A,\qquad M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A . $$

Thus $D(s)=(d_{A,B})$ is the INVERSE of $R(s)$, not its transpose. Also
$P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$.

**(i)** For every Specht label $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ and every simple label
$A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $[S(B):D(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$.

**(ii)** In the usual Specht-row/simple-column notation the rectangular
decomposition matrix is the transpose of $D$ restricted to standard rows; it is
NOT the transpose of the $L$-in-$M$ chart. The full matrix $D$ is unitriangular
on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, and its square submatrix on standard columns is
unitriangular; in particular $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ only for
$B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, since for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ the object
$D(B)=0$ is not a simple module label.

**(iii)** Retain the type-$A$ polynomial formula: for the right place action,
$w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the ENTRY stabilizer $K$,
$d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, and

$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}),$$

while the COLUMN Levi $J$ is a distinct group; the mixed singular/parabolic
composition matrix is the finite Levi cancellation sum over $C$ column-equivalent
to $B$, $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$, and equals
$d_{A,B}(1)$. All categorification multiplicities are ungraded at parameter
one, with the source/library reciprocal convention.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The two charts are mutually inverse.** By [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] the vectors $L_B$ and $M_A$ are two $\mathbb Z[s,s^{-1}]$-bases of the finite weight spaces of the Fock module, so the transition matrices $R(s)=(p_{A,B}(-s))$ with $L_B=\sum_AR_{A,B}(s)M_A$ and $D(s)=(d_{A,B})$ with $M_B=\sum_Ad_{A,B}(s)L_A$ satisfy $R(s)D(s)=D(s)R(s)=1$; both are triangular with diagonal entries $1$ on each weight block, and the quasi-canonical vector is $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(s)M_B$. The polynomial entries and the chart conventions are those of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]. [given, algebra]

1.2 **The type-$A$ polynomial dictionary.** The explicit transition coefficients are given by the type-$A$ formulas of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]]: for the right place action, $w_A$ is the shortest sorting element on the RIGHT of the entry stabilizer $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest on the LEFT, $p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2})$, the column Levi $J$ is distinct from $K$, and the mixed singular/parabolic composition coefficient is the finite Levi cancellation sum $\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$. [given, construct]

2.1 **The O-side multiplicity dictionary.** On the category-O side the standard module $N(B)$ has a composition series whose multiplicities with respect to the simples $L(A)$ are read off in the same chart: the coefficient of $M_B$ in the expansion of $P_A$ is the multiplicity of $L(A)$ in $N(B)$ at parameter one, in the source's reciprocal convention, by [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; combined with step 1.1 this gives $[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for all $A,B$, with $d_{A,B}$ unitriangular, and $[N(B):L(B)]=1$ for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ in the full square matrix. [step 1.1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 **Transfer to the Hecke side.** By [F2] the Schur quotient is exact, sends $N(B)$ to $S(B)$, $L(A)$ to $D(A)$ for standard $A$ and kills the off-standard simples; applying it to a composition series of $N(B)$ and using [F1] gives $[S(B):D(A)]=[N(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, the sum being finite on each weight block. This proves (i). [F2, step 2.1, F1, given]

4.1 **Shape of the matrix.** The full matrix $D=(d_{A,B})$ is unitriangular on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1; restricting rows to the simple labels $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ (all of which occur, and which index the simples by [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]) leaves a rectangular matrix, whose square submatrix on the standard columns is again unitriangular with diagonal entries $1$. The supported weight blocks and labels agree under the actual arbitrary-$I$ cut maps of the $G_0$ theorem, so this same coefficient calculation applies to every admitted consecutive interval. Off standard columns the equation $D(B)=0$ says precisely that $D(B)$ is not a simple module label, so the identity $[S(B):D(B)]=1$ is asserted only for $B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. This proves (ii). The statement is not that the rectangular matrix is invertible, and no off-standard simple is created. [step 3.1, given, algebra]

5.1 **The polynomial coefficient is not a transposed inverse.** In the coefficient convention used in the proof, the decomposition array has rows the simple labels and columns the Specht labels, and its entries are the coefficients of $D(s)$ at $s=1$; since $R(s)=D(s)^{-1}$, its transpose is $D(s)^{-t}$, which is in general different from the $L$-in-$M$ chart $R(s)$. On the two-factor space with labels $01<10$ one has $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$, so $R_{01,10}=-s$ is the negative-entry chart, whereas its inverse has $D_{01,10}=s$, while the true decomposition entry is $d_{01,10}(1)=1$: $S(10)$ is the simple $D(01)$ and not a formal negative combination. Hence with simple rows and Specht columns the decomposition matrix is the standard-row restriction of $D$; with Specht rows and simple columns it is its transpose. Neither convention uses the transpose of $R$. This completes (iii) together with steps 1.2, whose entry stabilizer $K$ and column Levi $J$ remain distinct and whose multiplicities are the finite Levi cancellation values at parameter one; all statements are ungraded. [step 3.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎
